clue.text: Honest, as we must be when the judge appears!

definitions.meaning: a person of integrity is described as decent and respectable in this sense

definitions.text: as we must be when the judge appears!
definitions.meaning: everyone in a courtroom rises to their feet when the judge enters

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition describes the courtroom custom of 'All rise': everyone is on their feet as the judge comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An honest, decent citizen is called upright in character; the same word also describes being on one's feet.

clue.text: All set, having shaved in advance

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before, in advance
pared means shaved or trimmed thin

explanation.surface: A man is ready to go, having shaved beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: To be prepared is to be ready, all set to go.

clue.text: Raised objection regarding subject of Swift's tale

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upward, bottom to top

parts.note: a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Someone objected to the topic of a story by Jonathan Swift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns BUT upward in this down entry. Jonathan Swift wrote the satire A Tale of a Tub (1704).
explanation.definitionFit: A Tub is named in the title of Swift's satire A Tale of a Tub, so it is literally the tale's subject.

clue.text: Bond's flair for discovering love in this

indicators.note: love is placed inside the word for flair

parts.note: a nose for something is a talent for sniffing it out
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: James Bond has a nose for finding romance here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond's' looks like the spy's possessive but is 'Bond has'; 'in' puts O inside NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope used to bind or tie, a kind of bond.

clue.text: Drinker's claim to be Bohemian composer

parts.note: saying 'I'm' is claiming to be something
Heinrich Biber was a 17th-century violinist-composer born in Bohemia

explanation.surface: A tippler boasts of being an artistic musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bohemian' looks like a free-spirited lifestyle, but it means from Bohemia, home of the Baroque composer Biber.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who imbibes is a drinker, usually of alcohol.

clue.text: Country festivity involving university curling team

indicators.note: the festivity surrounds, or takes in, the other pieces

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration

indicators.note: the word team is twisted out of its order

explanation.surface: A national celebration includes a college team playing the ice sport of curling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curling' is not the ice sport here: it twists the team's letters into ATEM, and 'involving' wraps the festivity round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala is a country in Central America.

clue.text: Collision that's made most of the papers

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: bumpf is British slang for paperwork, tedious documents

explanation.surface: A crash so dramatic it filled nearly every newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made most of' drops the last letter F from BUMPF, the British slang word for boring paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump is a minor collision, as when cars knock into each other.

clue.text: Additional fare here? It might be a bloomer

definitions.text: Additional fare here? It might be a bloomer

parts.words: Additional fare here? It might be a bloomer
parts.note: bakers traditionally threw in a thirteenth loaf as extra; a bloomer is a British loaf, not a mistake

explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a crusty British loaf; the extra loaf is the 'additional fare' given with twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means thirteen, from bakers adding a free loaf to every twelve sold.

clue.text: Again assimilate sailor into soldiers' sphere

indicators.note: the sailor is put into the soldiers' abbreviation, before its possessive S

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of British soldiers, and the possessive adds S
AB is an able-bodied seaman
an orb is a globe or sphere

explanation.surface: A navy man is absorbed back into an army's sphere of influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the sailor sitting inside the soldiers, whose possessive 's supplies a letter of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To reabsorb something is to take it in, or assimilate it, a second time.

clue.text: Deposited in bank, a rajah's capital

indicators.note: the answer is lodged inside the following words, as money is deposited in a bank

explanation.surface: An Indian prince's money has been paid into a bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposited in' signals letters lying within 'bANK A RAjah's'; 'capital' looks as if it means the rajah's wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital city of Turkey.

clue.text: Alley possibly used by sculptors?

definitions.meaning: an alley is a large glass or stone ball used in a children's rolling game
statues are commonly carved from this polished stone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Alley' looks like a lane, but it is a large playing marble; 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley is one type of glass toy ball, and sculptors carve the same-named stone.

clue.text: Representative needs supporter outside judiciary

indicators.note: the supporter goes around the judiciary

parts.note: a backer supports a person or project
the bench is the collective term for judges

explanation.surface: An elected member needs a sponsor outside the law courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the supporter round the judiciary; 'Representative' looks like a describing word but names an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A backbencher is a Member of Parliament without ministerial office, an elected representative.

clue.text: Food always kept outside tradesmen's entrance in sack

indicators.note: the inner construction is placed inside the word for sack

parts.note: to give someone the boot is to sack them

indicators.note: the word for always surrounds the following letter

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Provisions are stored out by the back door of a shop, in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tradesmen's entrance' looks like a back door, but 'entrance' just gives T; 'kept outside' makes EETR, and 'in' lodges that within the sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetroot is a red root vegetable eaten as food.

clue.text: Female footballer carrying keys from now on

indicators.note: the female and footballer together hold the keys between them

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
a forward is an attacking football player
C and E are two musical keys

explanation.surface: A woman footballer runs onto the pitch with a bunch of keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' has the two outer words hold the keys; a footballer who plays up front is the piece wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Henceforward is a formal adverb meaning starting now and continuing into the future.

clue.text: Make note about time in cheese-producing area

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: about and time go inside the cheese area

parts.note: Brie is a region of France famous for its cheese
CA is circa, meaning about

explanation.surface: A musician writes something about the timing in a French dairy region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' lodges about plus time within the French cheese region; 'note' looks like a written memo but is a sol-fa syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To fabricate is to make or construct something, sometimes falsely.

clue.text: Athenian statesman roughly repels Ionic extremists

indicators.note: roughly means the letters are rearranged in an approximate order
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Greek leader fends off radicals from Ionia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' takes I and C, the first and last letters of Ionic; 'roughly' mixes them with REPELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pericles led Athens during its golden age in the fifth century BC.

clue.text: Attractive girl failing to dip lights for police

parts.note: a bobby is a British police officer
headlights that are not dipped dazzle oncoming drivers, so such a driver is a dazzler

explanation.surface: A motorist who won't dip their headlights is reported to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is British slang for a police officer; drivers who keep headlights on full beam dazzle others.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobby-dazzler is old British slang for something or someone strikingly attractive, especially a pretty girl.

clue.text: Food you originally placed on trough for processing

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word
the word trough is processed, or rearranged

explanation.surface: Your dinner was put in the feeding trough to be prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives Y; 'for processing' rearranges TROUGH; 'placed on' sets Y above it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoghurt is a food made from fermented milk.

clue.text: In class it's hard to be modest

indicators.note: the letter for hard is placed inside the word for class

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social class
H stands for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: It's hard to be humble in a class at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts H inside CASTE, after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and restrained, which overlaps with modest in behaviour or dress.

clue.text: Rational article about cuttlefish product

indicators.note: the article goes around the cuttlefish product

parts.note: an article is an object, a thing
cuttlefish squirt ink as a defence

explanation.surface: Someone sensibly considers the uses of the sepia a cuttlefish produces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the article enclose the cuttlefish's defensive squirt; 'article' tempts towards A or THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinking person is reasoning, rational, using the mind.

clue.text: Unendingly sick, with fast pulse

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Feeling slightly unwell while fasting, someone has a racing heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unendingly' drops the last L of ILL to leave IL. 'pulse' wants to be a heartbeat; it is an edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the edible seeds of legumes, and the lentil is one of them.

clue.text: One who regularly fails the Spanish queen

parts.note: los is a Spanish word for the (masculine plural)
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A failure is attributed to the Queen of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letters signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone who habitually fails.

clue.text: Island one's annexed to church and state

parts.note: one is I, and the 's adds S
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa, a US state

explanation.surface: A territory is taken over by both church and the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Ischia is a volcanic island in the Bay of Naples, Italy.

clue.text: Wobbly, lacking capacity to cross public way

indicators.note: the word for lacking capacity spans the public way, holding it inside

parts.note: someone unable lacks the capacity to do something
ST is short for street, a public road

explanation.surface: Unsteady on their feet, a drinker can't manage to cross the road from the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cross' has the phrase for lacking capacity span the street abbreviation; the newspaper OCR showed 'public' as 'pub-lie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unstable is not steady, so it wobbles.

clue.text: Simple composition's distinctive quality

explanation.definitionFit: An air is a simple tune, and also an impression or quality someone gives off.

clue.text: One who succeeds? Sounds like 24

indicators.note: the answer is pronounced the same as the entry referred to

parts.note: the answer to 24 down, a tune or melody

explanation.surface: Someone who inherits is a homophone of another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 down is AIR; with a silent H, the answer is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir succeeds to a title or estate, so 'one who succeeds' is witty: not a winner but a successor.

clue.text: Record pay increase covering power project

indicators.note: the record and pay increase together enclose the letter for power

parts.note: to enter data is to record it
a rise is a British term for a raise in salary
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A record pay rise is part of a power station development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' has the record and pay rise close round the power symbol. 'Record' looks like an adjective, best ever; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is an undertaking or project, especially a bold one.
